scope: Numbers 7–8, all 115 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 7–8. All 115 exact original records are hashed, including source annotations at 7:4, 7:32, 7:40, 7:55, 7:59 and 7:68. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the completion setting and both acts of anointing and consecration; divide the sanctuary and altar objects into two readable sentences.
verses.before: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it with all its furnishings, and the altar with all its utensils; he anointed them and consecrated them.
verses.after: When Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and made it holy, along with all its furnishings. He also anointed the altar and all its utensils and made them holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it with all its furnishings, and the altar with all its utensils; he anointed them and consecrated them.

verses.rationale: Identify the leaders through the source’s household, tribe and census roles; make the repeated identifying clauses a connected explanation.
verses.before: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, made offerings. They were the leaders of the tribes, the ones who had overseen the counting.
verses.after: Then Israel’s leaders brought their offerings. These were the heads of their ancestral households, the tribal leaders who supervised the census.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, made offerings. They were the leaders of the tribes, the ones who had overseen the counting.

verses.rationale: Preserve six/twelve and two-leader/one-leader allocation; render tsab as covered with uncertainty noted rather than inventing a construction design.
verses.before: They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen—one wagon from every two leaders and one ox from each. They presented them before the tabernacle.
verses.after: Their offering before the LORD was six covered carts and twelve oxen: one cart for every two leaders and one ox from each leader. They brought them to the front of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen—one wagon from every two leaders and one ox from each. They presented them before the tabernacle.

verses.rationale: Retain the speech introduction and named recipient; exact source hash includes its accent annotation.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Connect acceptance to its purpose and resolve the distribution idiom by each man’s service requirements, preserving male Levite scope.
verses.before: “Accept these from them, so that they may be used for the service of the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to their service.”
verses.after: “Accept these from them for the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, assigning to each man what his work requires.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Accept these from them, so that they may be used for the service of the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to their service.”

verses.rationale: Keep both receipt and transfer; distributed expresses the allocation subsequently itemized.
verses.before: So Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
verses.after: Moses accepted the carts and oxen and distributed them to the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.

verses.rationale: Retain two carts/four oxen and the workload rationale, with sons of Gershon expressed as the clan name.
verses.before: He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites according to their service.
verses.after: He assigned two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for the work they had to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites according to their service.

verses.rationale: Retain four/eight and Ithamar’s oversight; the hand idiom names authority without suggesting ownership.
verses.before: He gave four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
verses.after: He assigned four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for the work they had to do, under Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gave four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserve the exclusion and its reason, with the imperfect as required customary carrying; no suggestion that carts were withheld as punishment.
verses.before: But to the Kohathites he gave none, because their service concerned the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.
verses.after: But he gave none to the Kohathites. They were responsible for the holy things and had to carry them on their shoulders.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the Kohathites he gave none, because their service concerned the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.

verses.rationale: Keep both presentations and the anointing setting; do not impose a chronology beyond the source.
verses.before: The leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed; the leaders brought their offering before the altar.
verses.after: The leaders brought offerings for the altar’s dedication when it was anointed. They brought their offerings before the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed; the leaders brought their offering before the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserve the doubled distributive phrase that establishes the twelve-day rhythm, using a dash for audible emphasis.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “One leader each day will bring an offering for the dedication of the altar.”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “One leader each day—one leader each day—is to bring his offering for the altar’s dedication.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “One leader each day shall bring an offering for the dedication of the altar.”

verses.rationale: Keep the first-day position, Nahshon son of Amminadab and Judah; Nahshon is not explicitly called leader in this verse.

verses.rationale: For Judah on day 1, preserve the two silver vessels, their separate 130/70 weights, sanctuary standard, and both fillings. Split the weight list from its contents without shortening the repeated offering.

verses.rationale: Resolve with him as the LORD and take the final speaking subject as divine, while noting the possible Moses subject; retain voice, precise location and atonement cover/testimony terms. No emendation of the pinned participle is required for speaking.
verses.before: When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And the LORD spoke to him.
verses.after: When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the atonement cover on the ark of the testimony, between the two cherubim. The LORD spoke to him there.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And the LORD spoke to him.

verses.rationale: Identify the divine speaker and Moses as recipient, introducing the nested instruction to Aaron.

verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Render raising the lamps as lighting with setting up noted as an alternative; keep seven and direction without inventing a particular geometry.
verses.before: “Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps will give light toward the front of the lampstand.”
verses.after: “Tell Aaron, ‘When you light the lamps, the seven lamps are to shine toward the area in front of the lampstand.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light toward the front of the lampstand.”

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated direction and command-fulfillment formula; Aaron remains the actor and Moses the command recipient.
verses.before: Aaron did so. He set up its lamps toward the front of the lampstand, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Aaron did this. He lit the lamps so they shone toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron did so. He set up its lamps toward the front of the lampstand, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserve the whole-work span and repeated hammered description; use passive for the unnamed maker rather than assigning fabrication to Moses.
verses.before: This was the workmanship of the lampstand: hammered work of gold, from its base to its blossoms it was hammered work. According to the pattern that the LORD showed Moses, so he made the lampstand.
verses.after: The lampstand was made of hammered gold, hammered from its base to its flowers. It was made according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the workmanship of the lampstand: hammered work of gold, from its base to its blossoms it was hammered work. According to the pattern that the LORD showed Moses, so he made the lampstand.

verses.rationale: Retain the new divine speech introducing Levite purification.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserve removal from the larger people for purification; do not equate ritual purity with absence of moral fault.
verses.before: “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.
verses.after: “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.

verses.rationale: Distinguish Moses sprinkling from the Levites shaving and washing; retain all flesh scope and avoid inventing the water’s ingredients.
verses.before: Thus you will do to them for their cleansing: sprinkle purifying water on them, and let them pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and cleanse themselves.
verses.after: This is how you are to purify them: sprinkle them with purification water. They are to shave their whole bodies, wash their clothes and purify themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall do to them for their cleansing: sprinkle purifying water on them, and let them pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and cleanse themselves.

verses.rationale: Preserve the switch from they to you, both bulls, the grain contents and the second bull’s sin-offering designation.
verses.before: Then they will take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you will take a second young bull for a sin offering.
verses.after: They are to take a young bull, with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they shall take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you shall take a second young bull for a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keep Moses’ two commands and the entire community without silently substituting representatives.
verses.before: You will bring the Levites before the Tent of Meeting and assemble the whole congregation of the Israelites.
verses.after: Bring the Levites to the front of the tent of meeting and gather the whole Israelite community.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bring the Levites before the Tent of Meeting and assemble the whole congregation of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Keep the people as hand-laying agents and the Levites as recipients; do not assert an unstated representative procedure.
verses.before: When you bring the Levites before the LORD, the Israelites will lay their hands on the Levites,
verses.after: Bring the Levites before the LORD. The Israelites are to lay their hands on the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you bring the Levites before the LORD, the Israelites shall lay their hands on the Levites,

verses.rationale: Preserve wave offering applied to people and its source/purpose; present avoids asserting a physical lifting procedure the passage does not explain.
verses.before: and Aaron will elevate the Levites before the LORD as an elevation offering from the Israelites, so that they may perform the service of the LORD.
verses.after: Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, so they can carry out the LORD’s work.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Aaron shall elevate the Levites before the LORD as an elevation offering from the Israelites, so that they may perform the service of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the second hand-laying stage, distinct actors, two offering assignments and atonement for the Levites; retain command to Moses rather than silently replacing him with Aaron.
verses.before: The Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
verses.after: The Levites are to lay their hands on the bulls’ heads. Offer one bull to the LORD as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.

verses.rationale: Retain the addressed Moses’ presentation and priestly recipients as written; do not collapse into the Aaron instruction in verse 11.
verses.before: You will have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and elevate them as an elevation offering to the LORD.
verses.after: Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons, and present them as a wave offering to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and elevate them as an elevation offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Make the result of separation audible while retaining divine possession and the Levites’ repeated designation.
verses.before: Thus you will separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
verses.after: In this way you are to separate the Levites from the rest of the Israelites. The Levites will belong to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites shall be mine.

verses.rationale: Preserve after this and the repeated purification/presentation instruction without fabricating a second ceremony.
verses.before: After that the Levites may enter to serve the Tent of Meeting, when you have cleansed them and elevated them as an elevation offering.
verses.after: After this, the Levites may enter to serve at the tent of meeting. You must purify them and present them as a wave offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: After that the Levites may enter to serve the Tent of Meeting, when you have cleansed them and elevated them as an elevation offering.

verses.rationale: Render the doubled given as wholly; retain replacement, male firstborn scope and the womb image rather than reducing it to eldest regardless of maternal birth order.
verses.before: For they are wholly given to me from among the Israelites. In place of every one who opens the womb, every firstborn among the Israelites, I have taken them for myself.
verses.after: For they are given wholly to me from among the Israelites. I have taken them for myself in place of every firstborn son of Israel, everyone who first opens the womb.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they are wholly given to me from among the Israelites. In place of every one who opens the womb, every firstborn among the Israelites, I have taken them for myself.

verses.rationale: Keep both human and animal firstborn and divine agency in Egypt’s deaths; retain sanctification to God without softening the harm.
verses.before: For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them for myself.
verses.after: Every firstborn among the Israelites belongs to me, human and animal alike. When I struck down every firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart as holy for myself.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them for myself.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated substitution, rather than deleting it as already explained.
verses.before: I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.
verses.after: I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Divide the long clause while retaining all five mentions of Israelites, divine gift, priestly recipients, service, atonement and the plague-prevention purpose; do not recast Levites as sacrificing priests.
verses.before: I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service of the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague may strike the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”
verses.after: From among the Israelites I have given the Levites to Aaron and his sons as a gift. They are to do the Israelites’ work at the tent of meeting and make atonement for the Israelites, so no plague strikes the Israelites when the Israelites approach the sanctuary.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service of the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague may strike the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”

verses.rationale: Keep all three participating parties and the repeated fulfillment statement; the Levites remain the object of the action.
verses.before: Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites did this to the Levites. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the Israelites did to them.
verses.after: Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite community did this with the Levites. The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses concerning them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites did this to the Levites. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the Israelites did to them.

verses.rationale: Distinguish self-purification from Aaron’s presentation and atonement, preserving his repeated name and purification as purpose.
verses.before: The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes; Aaron elevated them as an elevation offering before the LORD, and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.
verses.after: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD, and Aaron made atonement for them to purify them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes; Aaron elevated them as an elevation offering before the LORD, and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.

verses.rationale: Keep entry only after the ceremony and before Aaron as service under his oversight; use passive for the unspecified final they.
verses.before: Afterward the Levites entered to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting before Aaron and his sons. As the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
verses.after: Afterward the Levites entered the tent of meeting to carry out their work under Aaron and his sons. Everything was done for the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward the Levites entered to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting before Aaron and his sons. As the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.

verses.rationale: Retain the separate speech boundary introducing ages and work.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserve twenty-five instead of harmonizing chapter 4’s thirty; express the service-company idiom while retaining male eligibility.
verses.before: “This concerns the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they will enter to participate in the service at the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: “This is the rule for the Levites: from the age of twenty-five, a man is to join the company serving at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This concerns the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they shall enter to participate in the service at the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keep mandatory withdrawal at fifty and cessation of the specified service, preparing for the narrower continuing role in verse 26.
verses.before: At fifty years old they will withdraw from the work of the service and will serve no longer.
verses.after: At fifty he must withdraw from that company’s work and no longer perform it.
verses.tsw_comparator: At fifty years old they shall withdraw from the work of the service and shall serve no longer.

verses.rationale: Preserve assistance and keeping charge alongside the prohibition on work; do not claim total exclusion or invent a precise light-work/heavy-work division.
verses.before: They may assist their brothers at the Tent of Meeting in keeping charge, but they will perform no service. Thus you will do concerning the Levites and their responsibilities.”
verses.after: He may assist his fellow Levites at the tent of meeting in keeping its charge, but he must not perform the work. This is how you are to arrange the Levites’ duties.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They may assist their brothers at the Tent of Meeting in keeping charge, but they shall perform no service. Thus you shall do concerning the Levites and their responsibilities.”
